campaign.topic: S1-006 QA2 execution backend in process versus durable engine

claims.text: Design obligation / limit: results are model-based on a same-host research station with measured parameters; no production engine was installed; multi-host partition and vendor timer behaviour remain unknown; no production SLO is derived from S1-002/S1-004/S1-005 PASS_WITH_LIMITS.

Fact: all three adversarial probes are detected fail-closed through real simulation and evaluation paths: unsafe resume (probe A) FAILs on duplicate effect/receipt; incomparable workload (probe B) is INCOMPARABLE/NO_DATA and can never win; blind retry (probe C) FAILs without reconciliation evidence.

Research target: choose exactly one execution-backend direction with assumptions, non-goals, rollback path and a measurable migration trigger, without weakening gateway-only effects, fencing, transition+audit atomicity or reconciliation.

Dependency gate: S1-002 (revision 1, pass_with_limits) and S1-005 (revision 7, pass_with_limits) verified from actual bytes: tracked evidence packs, file/payload SHA-256, canonical DB evaluation ids, artifact chains and docs status all agree.

Derived verdict: PASS_WITH_LIMITS - recommendation 'in_process' with normalized scores in_process {'crash_recovery_time': 4, 'throughput_latency': 4, 'duplicate_effect_prevention': 4, 'unknown_outcome_reconciliation': 4, 'lease_fencing_stale_owner': 4, 'checkpoint_integrity_resume': 4, 'dag_determinism': 4, 'test_determinism_replay': 4, 'task_run_durability': 3, 'operator_visibility_complexity': 4, 'migration_reversibility': 4} vs durable_engine {'crash_recovery_time': 0, 'throughput_latency': 1, 'duplicate_effect_prevention': 4, 'unknown_outcome_reconciliation': 4, 'lease_fencing_stale_owner': 4, 'checkpoint_integrity_resume': 4, 'dag_determinism': 4, 'test_determinism_replay': 4, 'task_run_durability': 4, 'operator_visibility_complexity': 2, 'migration_reversibility': 2}; sensitivity stable across 222 deterministic runs (weight perturbations + seeded random vectors); independent rerun in a separate process and output directory reproduces the safety verdict within the frozen tolerance.

Measurement: over the frozen matrix (90 main runs) the in-process backend shows scheduling p95 4.86 us and recovery median 12000.0 us; the durable-engine model shows p95 25.71 us and recovery median 105000.0 us (lease timeout assumption); all safety counters are zero on every accepted run.

Inference: a durable engine preserves AgentOS semantics only as a single-writer stateful component with the transactional outbox and event-history dedup inside its state boundary; vendor-specific timer/replay semantics remain unknown without a vendor contract.

limitations: Model-based comparison on a same-host research station; durable-engine costs use documented assumptions (lease timeout 100 ms), no vendor engine was installed.
The runner implements the AgentOS contract, not a deployed production backend; no production SLO or availability claim is derived from S1-002/S1-004/S1-005 evidence.
Producer and verifier labels are process-separated roles in one local environment, not external human auditors.
Multi-host partition behaviour and vendor timer semantics are unknown and excluded from scoring.
Migration triggers are symbolic until the follow-up benchmark measures them.
